 140: const treeSitterParseTimeout = 5 * time.Second
 141: 
 142: // maxParseWalkDepth bounds every recursive walk this package performs over a
 143: // tree-sitter parse tree while parsing a file: the entity walk and the helpers
 144: // it calls, the pre-parse Rust unwrap pass that runs before it, and the
 145: // error-detail walk that runs after it. The full inventory, and the walkers
 146: // deliberately left out of it, is in the "Walk inventory" comment below.
 147: //
 148: // Tree-sitter builds its tree iteratively on the C heap, so a source file can
 149: // nest as deeply as it has bytes for; the Go walkers over that tree recurse once
 150: // per level. Neither guard in front of the parser catches it: 900k nested
 151: // parentheses is 1.8 MB, well under defaultMaxParseBytes (4 MiB), and one
 152: // character per line so looksMinified's 5000-column test never fires. A Go stack
 153: // overflow is a fatal, unrecoverable process abort that recover() cannot catch,
 154: // so this has to be a LIMIT applied before recursing, not a rescue afterwards.
 155: //
 156: // The number: every walk below was instrumented and re-measured over 56,261 real
 157: // source files, in two corpora measured separately. First-party (entire-graph,
 158: // cli, entire-api, entiredb, entire.io/{frontend,api}/src, entire.io/website;
 159: // 7,515 files): p99=33, p99.9=46, max 463 â€” generated Go protobuf,
 160: // entiredb gen/proto/publicapi/admin/v1/admin.pb.go. Third-party
 161: // (entire.io/node_modules; 48,746 files): p99=37, p99.9=184, max 418 â€”
 162: // iconv-lite/types/encodings.d.ts. Not one file was truncated at 5000.
 163: //
 164: // Deepest level any single walk reached, across both corpora:
 165: //
 166: //	walkEntitiesScoped 463   initializerTypeBodies 359   collectParseErrorDetails 310
 167: //	jsFunctionLikeNode  12   jsPatternBindingNames   8   firstNameDescendant       7
 168: //	firstDescendantOfType 2
 169: //
 170: // So 5000 is ~10x the deepest whole-file nesting anyone ships (generated
 171: // protobuf, generated .d.ts) and far more than that for the name-resolution
 172: // descents, which start at a declaration and only ever look downward. It caps
 173: // the walk at ~3.8 MB of stack (walkEntitiesScoped frames measured at 752 bytes
 174: // on darwin/arm64) against Go's 1 GB goroutine limit.
 175: //
 176: // Walk inventory. internal/sem contains exactly nine self-recursive functions
 177: // whose signature takes a *sitter.Node, plus three recursive closures over one
 178: // (enumerated mechanically over the package call graph, not by eye; no MUTUALLY
 179: // recursive node cycle exists). ALL TWELVE are bounded here â€” none is left out:
 180: //
 181: //	parser.go       walkEntitiesScoped, initializerTypeBodies' walk,
 182: //	                collectParseErrorDetails' walk, firstNameDescendant,
 183: //	                firstDescendantOfType, rAssignedValueKind,
 184: //	                unwrapRustItemWrapperMacros' walk
 185: //	js_scopes.go    jsPatternBindingNames, jsFunctionLikeNode â€” both reached
 186: //	                from walkEntitiesScoped through jsEntityParameterNames;
 187: //	                jsScopeWalker.walk, jsMemberChainParts â€” the relation phase,
 188: //	                which reparses the file and walks its own tree after the
 189: //	                entity phase has returned, so the entity budget never
 190: //	                reaches them
 191: //	parameters.go   identifierDescendants â€” reached from walkEntitiesScoped
 192: //	                through astParameterNames on every callable, BEFORE the walk
 193: //	                descends into it, so the walk's own budget is unspent and
 194: //	                cannot bound it
 195: //
 196: // identifierDescendants was the one walker an earlier revision of this change
 197: // left unbounded, on the evidence that three C declarator shapes (parenthesized,
 198: // pointer, array) nested to 800,000 levels never drove it deep. That evidence
 199: // was real but partial: C takes parameterBindingNames' `name` branch and never
 200: // the `pattern`/`declarator` branch, so it reads 0 levels at any nesting. Rust
 201: // and Python parameter PATTERNS take the other branch and descend one level per
 202: // source level â€” instrumented at 2,001 levels for a 2,000-level fixture â€” and
 203: // `fn f(&&&â€¦&a: u8) {}` aborts the process from ParseWithStatus. Two recursive
 204: // closures elsewhere in the package (kotlinReceiverTypeNames' visit, depth > 4;
 205: // uniqueImplementedMethod's walk, depth > 16) walk the SYMBOL graph rather than
 206: // a parse tree and carry their own explicit caps; they are not parse walkers and
 207: // are not governed by this limit.
 208: const maxParseWalkDepth = 5000
 209: 
 210: type ParseStatus struct {
 211: 	// ParseError reports that the parse did not fully succeed, so every
 212: 	// consumer surfaces a machine-readable warning for the file.
 213: 	ParseError bool
 214: 	// Partial reports that what WAS produced is nonetheless valid and usable:
 215: 	// the file parsed, the entities returned are real, and the only thing
 216: 	// missing is what the parser declined to reach. It separates a PARTIAL
 217: 	// RESULT from a TOTAL FAILURE, which are handled differently â€” a total
 218: 	// failure gives the diff no signal and suppresses the file's delta
 219: 	// (analyze.go), while a partial result keeps it. A partial result is still
 220: 	// a real coverage gap, so it counts toward completeness (provider.go);
 221: 	// that is what distinguishes it from an intentional skip, where the graph
 222: 	// chose not to look at the file at all.
 223: 	Partial bool
 224: 	// DepthExceeded reports that the AST walk hit maxParseWalkDepth,
 225: 	// independent of Partial: a tree that is both too deep AND malformed sets
 226: 	// this true while deliberately leaving Partial false (see the
 227: 	// depthExceeded && root.HasError() case below), because the malformed
 228: 	// tree's recovered entities may be wrong rather than merely incomplete.
 229: 	// Consumers that need to know specifically "was this side truncated by
 230: 	// the depth limit" â€” as opposed to "is what came back trustworthy" â€”
 231: 	// read this field, not Partial.
 232: 	DepthExceeded bool
 233: 	Code          string
 234: 	Detail        string
 235: }
 236: 
 237: func (TreeSitterParser) Parse(path, content string) ([]Entity, string) {
 238: 	entities, language, _ := TreeSitterParser{}.ParseWithStatus(path, content)
 239: 	return entities, language
 240: }
--- docs/brain-and-graph-boundaries.md ---
   1: # Entire Brain and Entire Graph boundaries
   2: 
   3: entire-graph is a **provider**: it turns a repository revision or working tree into a typed,
   4: no-egress snapshot and answers ranked queries over it. Entire Brain is the **consumer**: it ingests
   5: that snapshot alongside durable facts, sessions and checkpoints, and is where knowledge that is
   6: not reproducible from repository state belongs.
   7: 
   8: The line is not organizational; it is a property of the artifact. Facts derived from one requested
   9: repository state belong here, including explicitly labeled co-change relations from bounded Git
  10: history anchored at a revision. State accumulated across repositories, users, or independent runs
  11: belongs to Brain. Hidden provider state would make identical requests produce different results and
  12: weaken every downstream claim built on them.
  13: 
  14: This file exists so the items below are not re-litigated each time a competitor ships one.
  15: 
  16: ## The verdicts
  17: 
  18: ### MCP server surface â€” **Brain's job**
  19: An MCP surface adds client-facing tool, lifecycle, and policy decisions that are not graph facts.
  20: Entire Brain already owns that integration. The provider stays a one-shot, no-egress binary whose
  21: output is a stable NDJSON contract. Direct provider calls remain shell-outs; Entire Brain supplies
  22: the local MCP tool surface for clients that need one. That boundary is intentional, not a reason
  23: to grow a second server in this repository.
  24: 
  25: ### Multi-repo / cross-project graph â€” **Brain's job**
  26: `repoKey` is per-repository and every command takes one `--repo` on purpose. Committed-tree cache
  27: identity includes the repository, checkout, tree, profile, limits, selected files, and ignore
  28: inputs; there is no equivalent identity for "nine repositories as of roughly now." A merged
  29: cross-project graph is inherently a continuously reconciled store â€” Brain's shape, not a
  30: provider's. The provider's contribution is that its snapshots are cheap to ingest and its symbol
  31: IDs are stable, so N of them can be merged upstream.
  32: 
  33: ### save-result / reflect feedback loop â€” **Brain's job**
  34: A feedback loop is memory: outcomes recorded per user over time, decayed, corroborated, and fed
  35: back as a ranking overlay. Landing that here would make search results depend on who ran it and
  36: what they clicked last week â€” the exact opposite of the determinism the schema contract and every
  37: benchmark claim rest on. Brain is the correct home precisely because it is allowed to be stateful.
  38: If a learned overlay ever influences provider ranking, it must arrive as an explicit input to a
  39: query, never as hidden local state.
  40: 
  41: ### Human dashboards beyond a markdown report â€” **neither / not worth it**
  42: `index --report GRAPH_REPORT.md` is now in the provider, and it is the right amount: a
  43: deterministic, diffable, committable projection of a snapshot the tool already has in memory, which
  44: lets a human judge the tool in thirty seconds. An interactive HTML force-graph is not that. It is a
  45: UI product with its own rendering and performance envelope, it is unusable at the node counts this
  46: graph reaches on a real monorepo, and Brain's web surfaces are where an Entire user is already
  47: looking at their code. Building one here would be the most visible and least useful thing in this
  48: document.
  49: 
  50: ### Per-file incremental invalidation â€” **graph's job, not done yet**
  51: Tree-hash keying means a one-character commit pays a full rebuild. That is a provider concern
  52: (cache correctness and reuse of repository-derived facts) and it is the highest-value unbuilt item
  53: on this side of the line. It is unbuilt, not declined.
  54: 
  55: ### Watch mode / daemon â€” **neither / not worth it**
  56: Explicitly declined, and the reasoning holds: re-running `index` *is* the refresh, a changed tree
  57: misses the cache by construction, and a daemon would add an authoritative mutable process where
  58: the provider currently has only rebuildable derivative caches.
  59: 
  60: ### Named per-host installers â€” **graph's job, not done yet**
  61: `init-agents` writing `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` already covers the instruction-file hosts implicitly.
  62: Per-host installers are cheap, additive, and a real distribution win; they are simply not
  63: architecture, so they queue behind product behavior.
  64: 
  65: ## One-line test for anything new
  66: 
  67: Would this make two identical requests differ, or require mutable state that outlives one command?
  68: If yes, it is Brain's. If no, it is arguably ours â€” and then the only question is priority.
--- docs/commands.md ---
   1: # Command reference
   2: 
   3: Day to day, Entire Graph is driven by a coding agent following the guide that
   4: `init-agents` installs. The commands below are the same surface used directly
   5: for manual inspection, debugging a result the agent acted on, or scripting.
   6: `entire graph help` lists every public command for your installed version, and
   7: `entire graph <command> --help` is authoritative for flags; this page groups
   8: the commands by task and records the defaults that matter most.
   9: 
  10: Pass `--repo .` (or a path) when running outside an Entire session.
  11: 
  12: ## Set up
  13: 
  14: | Command | What it does |
  15: | --- | --- |
  16: | `init-agents` | Writes `.entire/graph-agent.md` and managed blocks in `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`. See [agent activation](agents.md). |
  17: | `agent-guide` | Prints the operating guide `init-agents` installs, for inspection or piping elsewhere. |
  18: | `index` | Prewarms one committed-tree cache variant before a batch of `--head` queries. Defaults to `--profile full`; see the [operations cache guide](operations.md#cache). |
  19: | `capabilities` | Reports semantic vs inventory-only languages, relation types, profiles, and features as JSON. Feature-detect with this before relying on a relation family. |
  20: 
  21: ## Inspect
  22: 
  23: These five form the interactive query family. They read the **working tree by
  24: default**; `--head` switches to the committed tree.
  25: 
  26: | Command | What it does |
  27: | --- | --- |
  28: | `search` | Ranked source regions for a plain-language query. Defaults: `--format json`, `--profile fast` (the installed agent guide asks for `--profile full`). Formats: `json`, `ndjson`, `text`, `agent`. See [search results](search.md). |
  29: | `def` | One name's declaration, fields, and method surface. Default format is text. |
  30: | `explain` | Resolves symbols named by a failing build or test into definitions and context. |
  31: | `neighbors` | Direct relations of one symbol (`--relation`, `--direction`, `--depth 1\|2`). Ambiguous names return a definition list; disambiguate with `--file`. |
  32: | `impact` | One-shot blast radius for a symbol: direct and transitive callers (depth â‰¤ 2), callees, type consumers, data flows, co-change files, siblings. |
  33: 
  34: Cache visibility differs by command and format. JSON from `search`, `impact`,
  35: and `neighbors` includes cache fields. Text output from `impact` and
  36: `neighbors` starts with an `Index: cache-hit` or `cache-miss` header. Agent
  37: output from `search` and `neighbors` normally uses that header, compacting it
  38: to `I:hit`/`I:miss` under a tight byte budget and potentially omitting it under
  39: an extreme cap. `search --format text` and `explain` report no cache state.
  40: `def` and `explain` also skip the per-user fallback cache directory that the
  41: other query commands use; details are in the
  42: [operations cache guide](operations.md#cache).
  43: 
  44: ## Analyze changes
  45: 
  46: | Command | What it does |
  47: | --- | --- |
  48: | `commit <ref>` | Entity-level change list for a commit vs its first parent, with heuristic dependent counts. |
  49: | `diff --base A --head B` | The same between two refs. `analyze` is an alias of `diff`. |
  50: | `checkpoint <id>` | Analyzes the commit behind an Entire-Checkpoint trailer. |
  51: | `verify` | Runs a caller-provided test command and returns an adjudicated verdict. This executes the command you pass it; see [trust and security](trust-and-security.md). |
  52: 
  53: ## Export
  54: 
  55: Bulk NDJSON streams. These default to the **committed tree**; pass
  56: `--worktree` to stream the working tree instead.
  57: 
  58: | Command | What it does |
  59: | --- | --- |
  60: | `snapshot` | The whole graph: header, files, externals, symbols, relations, summary. Also supports `--format compact-ndjson` and the experimental `--format scip`. |
  61: | `symbols` | Symbol records only. There is no name filter; grep the stream, or use `search`/`def` for a targeted lookup. |
  62: | `edges` | Relation records, filterable server-side with `--to`, `--from`, `--relation`. |
  63: | `snapshot-query` | Queries a saved compact snapshot without rebuilding the graph. |
  64: 
  65: Stream and record formats are specified in
  66: [snapshot format](snapshot-format.md).
  67: 
  68: ## Report
  69: 
  70: `stats` is a human-facing, read-only report of graph vs grep/read usage in
  71: local coding-agent transcripts, with an explicitly modeled (not measured)
  72: token-savings estimate. It is not part of the agent workflow; see
  73: [trust and security](trust-and-security.md) for what it reads.

   1: // entire-graph is an Entire CLI external command.

  15: var version = "dev"
  16: 
  17: func main() {
  18: 	if err := cli.Execute(version, os.Args[1:]); err != nil {
  19: 		// Escape by VALUE, not by wrapping os.Stderr. Error text is not
  20: 		// tool-authored - it carries pathnames from `git diff -z`, Git's own
  21: 		// stderr, and the argv gitutil's run() echoes back, and a Git pathname
  22: 		// may hold any byte but NUL and '/' - so an ESC, a C1 CSI or an LF in a
  23: 		// scanned repository would otherwise be obeyed by the reader's terminal
  24: 		// rather than displayed. A termsafe Writer around os.Stderr cannot be
  25: 		// used here for two reasons: stderr also carries the index progress
  26: 		// bar's own cursor control (internal/cli/progressbar.go writes
  27: 		// "\r...\033[K" to opts.Stderr), which a writer wrap could not tell
  28: 		// apart from an injected sequence; and Writer keeps LF as layout, which
  29: 		// is precisely the byte a one-line error report must not let a
  30: 		// repository forge. Line() is the same by-value treatment the other
  31: 		// stderr sink already uses for a repository-derived path
  32: 		// (internal/cli/root.go, diffProgressLine).
  33: 		//
  34: 		// ACCEPTED COST: Line() escapes LF and TAB, so a Git diagnostic that is
  35: 		// legitimately several lines would print on one line with its breaks
  36: 		// shown as \x0a rather than taken. No such diagnostic is reachable
  37: 		// through this sink today - every revision this tool resolves goes
  38: 		// through `git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options`, whose failures are
  39: 		// one terse line - but git's stderr is folded into these errors
  40: 		// verbatim, so a multi-line one is a change in a git version away. That
  41: 		// collapse is deliberate and cannot be avoided here: by the time a
  42: 		// hint's newline and an injected one are both bytes inside one error
  43: 		// string, nothing at this sink can tell which of them git wrote. A
  44: 		// one-line report that is honest about its breaks beats a multi-line
  45: 		// one a repository can append to.
  46: 		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, termsafe.Line(err.Error()))
  47: 		os.Exit(1)
  48: 	}
  49: }

 135: func runDoctor(ctx context.Context, opts Options, args []string) error {
 136: 	asJSON := false
 137: 	var asserts []string
 138: 	for index := 0; index < len(args); index++ {
 139: 		switch args[index] {
 140: 		case "--json":
 141: 			asJSON = true
 142: 		case "--assert":
 143: 			// Repeatable: a harness usually drives more than one verb, and finding out about the
 144: 			// second one only after the first has been fixed costs another whole run.
 145: 			if index+1 >= len(args) {
 146: 				return errors.New("doctor --assert needs a command line, for example --assert \"search --profile full\"")
 147: 			}
 148: 			index++
 149: 			asserts = append(asserts, args[index])
 150: 		default:
 151: 			return errors.New("doctor accepts only --json and --assert \"<command line>\"")
 152: 		}
 153: 	}
 154: 	// The assertions run FIRST and stop the report: a caller that asked whether this binary can
 155: 	// serve its command line wants that answer, and printing an otherwise-healthy environment
 156: 	// report above the failure buries it.
 157: 	for _, spec := range asserts {
 158: 		if err := checkPreflight(opts.Version, spec); err != nil {
 159: 			return err
 160: 		}
 161: 	}
 162: 	if len(asserts) > 0 && !asJSON {
 163: 		for _, spec := range asserts {
 164: 			fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stdout, "assert_ok=%q\n", spec)
 165: 		}
 166: 	}
 167: 	report := map[string]any{
 168: 		"provider":  sem.ProviderName,
 169: 		"version":   opts.Version,
 170: 		"no_egress": true,
 171: 		"environment": map[string]string{
 172: 			envCLIVersion:    valueOrUnset(opts.Env.CLIVersion),
 173: 			envRepoRoot:      valueOrUnset(opts.Env.RepoRoot),
 174: 			envPluginDataDir: valueOrUnset(opts.Env.PluginDataDir),
 175: 		},
 176: 		"phase_1_local_only": map[string]bool{
 177: 			"fetch_remote_code":              false,
 178: 			"download_grammars_or_assets":    false,
 179: 			"upload_telemetry":               false,
 180: 			"call_hosted_model_apis":         false,
 181: 			"call_remote_embedding_provider": false,
 182: 			"perform_network_discovery":      false,
 183: 		},
 184: 	}
 185: 	if len(asserts) > 0 {
 186: 		// Reaching here means every assertion parsed, so the JSON says so explicitly rather than
 187: 		// leaving a caller to infer success from the absence of an error.
 188: 		report["asserted_command_lines"] = asserts
 189: 	}
 190: 	if !asJSON {
 191: 		fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stdout, "ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION=%s\n", valueOrUnset(opts.Env.CLIVersion))
 192: 		fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stdout, "ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT=%s\n", valueOrUnset(opts.Env.RepoRoot))
 193: 		fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stdout, "ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR=%s\n", valueOrUnset(opts.Env.PluginDataDir))
 194: 		fmt.Fprintln(opts.Stdout, "no_egress=true")
 195: 	}
 196: 
 197: 	if opts.Env.PluginDataDir != "" {
 198: 		if err := os.MkdirAll(opts.Env.PluginDataDir, 0o700); err != nil {
 199: 			return fmt.Errorf("create plugin data dir: %w", err)
 200: 		}
 201: 		probe, err := os.CreateTemp(opts.Env.PluginDataDir, ".write-test-*")
 202: 		if err != nil {
 203: 			return fmt.Errorf("write plugin data dir: %w", err)
 204: 		}
 205: 		probeName := probe.Name()
 206: 		if err := probe.Close(); err != nil {
 207: 			return fmt.Errorf("close plugin data probe: %w", err)
 208: 		}
 209: 		if err := os.Remove(probeName); err != nil {
 210: 			return fmt.Errorf("remove plugin data probe: %w", err)
 211: 		}
 212: 		report["plugin_data_dir"] = "writable"
 213: 		if !asJSON {
 214: 			fmt.Fprintln(opts.Stdout, "plugin_data_dir=writable")
 215: 		}
 216: 	}

 218: 	repo, err := resolveRepo(ctx, opts.Env, "")

 228: 		report["repo_error"] = err.Error()

  20: // defaultSearchContextBytes is the default `--max-context-bytes` ceiling for one search call.
  21: //
  22: // It is sized by TURN economics, not by payload economics. Measured on real agentic sessions,
  23: // the search payload is ~0.6% of what a session spends, while a single extra agent turn costs
  24: // ~42.5k tokens (95.9% of billed tokens are context re-read). A search that stops one Read
  25: // short of an edit therefore costs about 40x more than the entire payload that caused it, so
  26: // the ceiling's job is NOT to be small â€” it is to never be the reason a head result comes back
  27: // as half a function.
  28: //
  29: // 24 kB â‰ˆ 6k tokens: it clears the largest ranked payloads observed (~15 kB) with room for the
  30: // five complete head bodies the allocator may buy, so the allocator is bounded by what bodies
  31: // actually cost rather than silently truncated by the ceiling. The old 16 kB default could not
  32: // fit even one complete body on top of a large ranking. In practice payloads do NOT expand to
  33: // fill it: the allocator only spends bytes on complete head bodies and always picks the
  34: // cheapest plan that delivers them (measured on a 14-repo probe: mean payload 11.8 kB, i.e.
  35: // half the ceiling). `--max-context-bytes` remains honored exactly, so a caller who wants the
  36: // old behaviour passes `--max-context-bytes 16384`.
  37: const defaultSearchContextBytes = 24 * 1024
  38: 
  39: // searchReferenceBlocks names the three off-by-default reference blocks. They are addressable
  40: // individually because they were measured individually: a caller who wants the navigation aid should
  41: // not have to pay for the declaration card as well.
  42: //
  43: // `all` is accepted as shorthand. An unknown name is an error rather than a silent no-op â€” a flag
  44: // that quietly does nothing is how a measurement gets attributed to the wrong build.
  45: const (
  46: 	searchReferenceBlockContainerMap   = "container-map"
  47: 	searchReferenceBlockSignatureTypes = "signature-types"
  48: 	searchReferenceBlockTypeCard       = "type-card"
  49: 	searchReferenceBlocksAll           = "all"
  50: )

  82: 	SingleResolution      bool
  83: 	DocumentResolution    bool
  84: 	// The reference blocks, off unless asked for. See SearchOptions in internal/sem/search.go for
  85: 	// the session measurement that made OFF the default.
  86: 	ContainerMap   bool
  87: 	SignatureTypes bool
  88: 	TypeCard       bool
  89: }
  90: 
  91: // applySearchReferenceBlocks turns a comma-separated block list into flags. It is used for both the
  92: // `--reference-blocks` flag and the ENTIRE_GRAPH_REFERENCE_BLOCKS environment variable, so the two
  93: // cannot drift.
  94: func applySearchReferenceBlocks(flags *searchFlags, value string) error {
  95: 	for _, name := range strings.Split(value, ",") {
  96: 		name = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(name))
  97: 		switch name {
  98: 		case "":
  99: 		case searchReferenceBlocksAll:
 100: 			flags.ContainerMap, flags.SignatureTypes, flags.TypeCard = true, true, true
 101: 		case searchReferenceBlockContainerMap:
 102: 			flags.ContainerMap = true
 103: 		case searchReferenceBlockSignatureTypes:
 104: 			flags.SignatureTypes = true
 105: 		case searchReferenceBlockTypeCard:
 106: 			flags.TypeCard = true
 107: 		default:
 108: 			return fmt.Errorf("unknown search reference block %q: want %s, %s, %s, or %s",
 109: 				name, searchReferenceBlockContainerMap, searchReferenceBlockSignatureTypes,
 110: 				searchReferenceBlockTypeCard, searchReferenceBlocksAll)
 111: 		}
 112: 	}
 113: 	return nil
 114: }

 116: func runSearch(ctx context.Context, opts Options, args []string) error {
 117: 	flags, rest, err := parseSearchFlags(args)
 118: 	if err != nil {
 119: 		return err
 120: 	}
 121: 	// The environment sets a session-wide default; the flags then add to it. A flag can only ever
 122: 	// turn a block ON, so the two compose without either having to override the other.
 123: 	if value := strings.TrimSpace(opts.Env.ReferenceBlocks); value != "" {
 124: 		if err := applySearchReferenceBlocks(&flags, value); err != nil {
 125: 			return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", envReferenceBlocks, err)
 126: 		}
 127: 	}
 128: 	if len(rest) != 0 {
 129: 		return unexpectedArgumentsError("search", opts.Version, rest)
 130: 	}
 131: 	if strings.TrimSpace(flags.Query) == "" {
 132: 		return errors.New("search requires --query")
 133: 	}
 134: 	// ZERO-TOLL DELIVERY. When the caller has already computed this session's payload and handed it
 135: 	// to the agent inside context the session pays for anyway, this call must cost nothing: echo
 136: 	// those bytes and return, before the profile, the repo, the cache and the index are touched.
 137: 	if path := strings.TrimSpace(opts.Env.PresearchPath); path != "" {
 138: 		return echoPresearchPayload(opts.Stdout, path)
 139: 	}
 140: 	// The echo is decided before any INDEXING work: a replayed payload must not pay for an index
 141: 	// build. See searchSession for what the cap is worth and why it is an echo.
 142: 	//
 143: 	// It does now pay for bounded tree, corpus-policy, and path-admissibility checks. Those checks
 144: 	// prove that the same committed identity and current effective corpus policy still admit every
 145: 	// recorded contributing path. Corpus broadening and worktree source bytes remain intentionally
 146: 	// session-stale, like the later query itself: this cap replays the first answer verbatim rather
 147: 	// than promising a fresh ranking. The checks stay deliberately ahead of the index build. See
 148: 	// searchSessionScope and sem.SearchReplayPolicy.
 149: 	session, err := newSearchSession(opts.Env, opts.Stderr)
 150: 	if err != nil {
 151: 		return err
 152: 	}
 153: 	profile, err := parseProfile(flags.Profile)
 154: 	if err != nil {
 155: 		return err
 156: 	}
 157: 	repo, err := resolveRepo(ctx, opts.Env, flags.Repo)
 158: 	if err != nil {
 159: 		return err
 160: 	}
 161: 	var (
 162: 		scope               searchSessionScope
 163: 		replayPolicy        sem.SearchReplayPolicy
 164: 		replayPolicyReady   bool
 165: 		forceSessionReplace bool
 166: 	)
 167: 	if session != nil {
 168: 		scope = searchSessionScopeFor(ctx, repo)
 169: 		scope.Format = flags.Format
 170: 		// A rendered payload is opaque: snippets and reference blocks cannot be safely removed from
 171: 		// it after the fact. Bind it to the semantic layer's effective corpus policy and validate
 172: 		// every contributing path before writing even the replay header. Policy resolution is an
 173: 		// optimization gate; failure declines the echo and lets the real search report any error.
 174: 		var (
 175: 			policy    sem.SearchReplayPolicy
 176: 			policyErr error
 177: 		)
 178: 		if flags.Worktree {
 179: 			// A mutable worktree cannot provide an immutable replay identity.
 180: 			// Skip the corpus-policy observation entirely; it cannot authorize a
 181: 			// replay and would add an unnecessary second filesystem traversal.
 182: 			forceSessionReplace = true
 183: 		} else {
 184: 			policy, policyErr = sem.ResolveSearchReplayPolicy(ctx, repo, sem.SearchOptions{
 185: 				Worktree:     false,
 186: 				IgnoreFiles:  flags.IgnoreFiles,
 187: 				IncludeFiles: flags.IncludeFiles,
 188: 			})
 189: 		}
 190: 		if policyErr == nil && !policy.MatchesTree(scope.Tree) {
 191: 			// Mutable worktree state cannot be pinned through the final
 192: 			// admission-to-output interval. Discard any payload written by an
 193: 			// older binary as the live search completes; retaining it would keep
 194: 			// credential-bearing bytes on disk even though this binary can never
 195: 			// safely replay them.
 196: 			forceSessionReplace = true
 197: 		}
 198: 		if policyErr == nil && policy.MatchesTree(scope.Tree) {
 199: 			replayPolicy = policy
 200: 			replayPolicyReady = true
 201: 			scope.PolicyFingerprint = policy.Fingerprint()
 202: 			state, ok := searchSessionState{}, false
 203: 			if searchFormatSupportsReplay(flags.Format) {
 204: 				state, ok = session.echo(scope)
 205: 			}
 206: 			if !ok && state.Payload != "" {
 207: 				forceSessionReplace = true
 208: 			}
 209: 			if ok {
 210: 				// Resolve both identities again immediately before output. This brackets the
 211: 				// candidate lookup with tree and policy observations, so a concurrent ref or
 212: 				// policy-file change declines replay instead of serving the earlier view.
 213: 				confirmedPolicy, confirmErr := sem.ResolveSearchReplayPolicy(ctx, repo, sem.SearchOptions{
 214: 					Worktree:     flags.Worktree,
 215: 					IgnoreFiles:  flags.IgnoreFiles,
 216: 					IncludeFiles: flags.IncludeFiles,
 217: 				})
 218: 				confirmedScope := searchSessionScopeFor(ctx, repo)
 219: 				confirmedScope.PolicyFingerprint = confirmedPolicy.Fingerprint()
 220: 				confirmedScope.Format = flags.Format
 221: 				if confirmErr == nil &&
 222: 					confirmedPolicy.Fingerprint() == replayPolicy.Fingerprint() &&
 223: 					confirmedPolicy.MatchesTree(confirmedScope.Tree) &&

 230: 						// not all part of the root-rule fingerprint.

 232: 							Worktree:     flags.Worktree,
 233: 							IgnoreFiles:  flags.IgnoreFiles,
 234: 							IncludeFiles: flags.IncludeFiles,
 235: 						})
 236: 						finalScope := searchSessionScopeFor(ctx, repo)

 139: func runNeighbors(ctx context.Context, opts Options, args []string) error {
 140: 	flags, err := parseNeighborFlags(args)
 141: 	if err != nil {
 142: 		return err
 143: 	}
 144: 	repo, err := resolveRepo(ctx, opts.Env, flags.Repo)
 145: 	if err != nil {
 146: 		return err
 147: 	}
 148: 	profile, err := parseProfile(flags.Profile)
 149: 	if err != nil {
 150: 		return err
 151: 	}
 152: 	cacheDir := resolveCacheDir(flags.CacheDir, opts.Env.PluginDataDir)
 153: 	totalStarted := time.Now()
 154: 	indexStarted := totalStarted
 155: 	snapshot, cacheHit, err := sem.LoadOrBuildProviderSnapshot(ctx, repo, opts.Version, sem.ProviderSnapshotOptions{
 156: 		NoNetwork:    true,
 157: 		Worktree:     flags.Worktree,
 158: 		IgnoreFiles:  flags.IgnoreFile,
 159: 		IncludeFiles: flags.IncludeFile,
 160: 		Profile:      profile,
 161: 	}, cacheDir, flags.DisableCache)
 162: 	if err != nil {
 163: 		return err
 164: 	}
 165: 	readSource, closeSource := openSnapshotLineReaderOrDegrade(ctx, snapshot, flags.Worktree, opts.Stderr)
 166: 	if closeSource != nil {
 167: 		defer closeSource()
 168: 	}
 169: 	indexLatency := time.Since(indexStarted)
 170: 	queryStarted := time.Now()
 171: 	response := buildNeighborResponseFromReader(snapshot, flags, readSource)
 172: 	// Call-site resolution reads the caller's source from the same snapshot-bound
 173: 	// reader as fuzzy and ambiguous bodies. It runs after the graph query and is
 174: 	// bounded by the answer's size.
 175: 	annotateNeighborCallSites(&response, readSource)
 176: 	queryLatency := time.Since(queryStarted)
 177: 	response.IndexCacheHit = cacheHit
 178: 	response.IndexCacheDisabled = cacheDir == "" || flags.DisableCache
 179: 	response.IndexLatencyMS = indexLatency.Milliseconds()
 180: 	response.QueryLatencyMS = queryLatency.Milliseconds()
 181: 	response.TotalLatencyMS = time.Since(totalStarted).Milliseconds()
 182: 	switch flags.Format {
 183: 	case "json":
 184: 		encoder := json.NewEncoder(termsafe.NewJSONWriter(opts.Stdout))
 185: 		encoder.SetEscapeHTML(false)
 186: 		return encoder.Encode(response)
 187: 	case "agent":
 188: 		return writeAgentNeighborsBounded(opts.Stdout, response, flags.MaxContextBytes)
 189: 	case "text":
 190: 		return writeAgentNeighbors(opts.Stdout, response)
 191: 	default:
 192: 		return fmt.Errorf("neighbors --format must be json, text, or agent, got %q", flags.Format)
 193: 	}
 194: }

 197: 	flags := neighborFlags{
 198: 		Format: "json", Profile: "full", Relation: "CALLS", Direction: "both",
 199: 		Depth: 1, Limit: defaultNeighborLimit, Worktree: true,

  19: // `def` â€” a structural declaration lookup
  20: // ======================================
  21: //
  22: // The question this answers is "what IS this name, and what can I do with it?".
  23: // Before it existed the only single-symbol lookups were relation queries
  24: // (`neighbors`, `impact`), so every consumer that wanted a declaration rolled
  25: // its own by grepping the `symbols` stream for a NAME SUBSTRING â€” and a
  26: // substring match over names is exactly how one type's members get reported as
  27: // another's: asking for `Edit` matched `edits`, so the answer to "what does
  28: // Edit have?" was two of Edit's fields followed by two members of Fix, with
  29: // every associated function in `impl Edit` missing.
  30: //
  31: // So membership here is never inferred from spelling. A member is a member
  32: // because the graph says so:
  33: //
  34: //   - a CONTAINS edge from the declaration (or a container_id pointing at it),
  35: //     which is where inherent `impl` blocks, Go receiver methods, Swift/Kotlin
  36: //     extensions and C# extension methods all land;
  37: //   - a member of a supertype the declaration EXTENDS/INHERITS/IMPLEMENTS,
  38: //     reported one hop only and labelled with where it came from (PHP traits,
  39: //     Ruby modules, base classes);
  40: //   - never a symbol whose name merely contains the query.

  42: // Partial declarations of one type (C# `partial class`) are merged, because they

  28: // The graph has taken essentially everything available in the locate phase; half of what remains is
  29: // the edit->build->fix loop, and the graph did nothing for it. The reason is not that the graph lacks
  30: // the answer â€” `def` has it â€” but that the agent never asks: offering `def` in the prompt for exactly
  31: // this case produced 0.04 calls per session across 28 sessions. Telling an agent to choose a tool
  32: // after its build fails does not work; it is already in the shell, so it greps.
  33: //
  34: // So this is not another instruction. It is a command that composes with the build in ONE shell call,
  35: // and the VERIFY block emits it pre-composed, so the agent runs the command it was given and the
  36: // declarations arrive with the failure:
  37: //
  38: //	go test ./internal/configs -run '^TestX$' 2>&1 | entire graph explain --repo .
  39: //
  40: // One turn replaces build -> grep symbol -> read range. It quotes no source it was not asked for and
  41: // it stays read-only: the build is run by the shell, not by this process, so the provider remains a
  42: // pure analyzer.
  43: const (
  44: 	// explainMaxSymbols bounds how many distinct names are resolved. A cascading build failure can
  45: 	// name hundreds; the first few are the cause and the rest are consequences.
  46: 	explainMaxSymbols = 8
  47: 
  48: 	// explainMaxBytes bounds the whole block, on the same reasoning as the search payload: bytes here
  49: 	// are replayed into the model on every later turn.
  50: 	explainMaxBytes = 2048
  51: )
  52: 
  53: // explainErrorPatterns are the ways compilers and test runners name a symbol they cannot resolve.
  54: // Each pattern captures ONE identifier. They are deliberately conservative: a pattern that also
  55: // matched ordinary prose would fill the block with words that are not symbols, which is strictly
  56: // worse than an empty block.
  57: var explainErrorPatterns = []*regexp.Regexp{
  58: 	// Go: "undefined: foo", "x.foo undefined (type T has no field or method foo)"
  59: 	regexp.MustCompile(`undefined:\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*)`),
  60: 	regexp.MustCompile(`has no field or method\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`),
  61: 	regexp.MustCompile(`declared and not used:\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`),
  62: 	// Rust: "cannot find function `foo`", "no method named `foo`", "unresolved import `a::b`"
  63: 	regexp.MustCompile("cannot find (?:function|value|type|struct|trait|macro)[^`]*`([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`"),
  64: 	regexp.MustCompile("no method named `([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`"),
  65: 	regexp.MustCompile("no field `([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`"),
  66: 	// Java / Kotlin: "cannot find symbol\n  symbol: method foo(int)"
  67: 	regexp.MustCompile(`symbol:\s+(?:method|variable|class)\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`),
  68: 	regexp.MustCompile(`cannot find symbol[^\n]*?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{2,})\s*\(`),
  69: 	// TypeScript / JavaScript: "Property 'foo' does not exist", "Cannot find name 'foo'"
  70: 	regexp.MustCompile(`Property '([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)' does not exist`),
  71: 	regexp.MustCompile(`Cannot find name '([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)'`),
  72: 	regexp.MustCompile(`([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*) is not defined`),
  73: 	regexp.MustCompile(`([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*) is not a function`),
  74: 	// Python: "AttributeError: 'T' object has no attribute 'foo'", "NameError: name 'foo' is not defined"
  75: 	regexp.MustCompile(`has no attribute '([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)'`),
  76: 	regexp.MustCompile(`name '([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)' is not defined`),
  77: 	// PHP: "Call to undefined method C::foo()"
  78: 	regexp.MustCompile(`Call to undefined (?:method|function)\s+(?:[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*::)?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`),
  79: 	// Ruby: "undefined method `foo' for"
  80: 	regexp.MustCompile("undefined (?:method|local variable or method) `([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_?!]*)'"),
  81: 	// Generic arity/type complaints that still name the callee.
  82: 	regexp.MustCompile(`(?:not enough|too many) arguments (?:in call to|to)\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*)`),
  83: }
  84: 
  85: // ExplainSymbol is one resolved declaration.
  86: type ExplainSymbol struct {
  87: 	Query     string `json:"query"`
  88: 	Name      string `json:"name,omitempty"`
  89: 	Kind      string `json:"kind,omitempty"`
  90: 	Signature string `json:"signature,omitempty"`
  91: 	FilePath  string `json:"file_path,omitempty"`
  92: 	StartLine int    `json:"start_line,omitempty"`
  93: 	EndLine   int    `json:"end_line,omitempty"`
  94: 	Owner     string `json:"owner,omitempty"`
  95: 	// Resolved is false when the error named something the graph does not index. Reported rather than
  96: 	// hidden: "the repository does not define this" is itself the answer the agent needs, and a silent
  97: 	// omission would read as "no information".
  98: 	Resolved bool `json:"resolved"`
  99: }
 100: 
 101: // ExplainResponse is the whole answer.
 102: type ExplainResponse struct {
 103: 	Symbols []ExplainSymbol `json:"symbols"`
 104: 	// Scanned is how many candidate names the error text yielded, so a truncated answer is visible.
 105: 	Scanned int `json:"scanned"`
 106: 	Omitted int `json:"omitted,omitempty"`
 107: 	// Commit / Tree / WorktreeSnapshot are the provenance of the declarations above: WHICH tree these
 108: 	// line numbers and signatures describe. The text form says it in its header; without these a JSON
 109: 	// consumer had no way to tell a --head answer from a working-tree one, and on a clean tree the two
 110: 	// were byte-identical. Same field names and semantics as def, neighbors, and impact.
 111: 	Commit           string `json:"commit,omitempty"`
 112: 	Tree             string `json:"tree,omitempty"`
 113: 	WorktreeSnapshot bool   `json:"worktree_snapshot,omitempty"`
 114: }
 115: 
 116: type explainFlags struct {
 117: 	Repo            string
 118: 	Profile         string
 119: 	CacheDir        string
 120: 	Format          string
 121: 	Worktree        bool
 122: 	DisableCache    bool
 123: 	MaxSymbols      int
 124: 	MaxContextBytes int
 125: 	// Echo passes stdin through before the block, so the command is a FILTER and can be baked into
 126: 	// the VERIFY line without hiding the test output it was piped from. --no-echo restores the
 127: 	// block-only form for callers that already have the output.
 128: 	Echo        bool
 129: 	IgnoreFile  []string
 130: 	IncludeFile []string
 131: }
 132: 
 133: func runExplain(ctx context.Context, opts Options, args []string) error {
 134: 	flags, err := parseExplainFlags(args)
 135: 	if err != nil {
 136: 		return err
 137: 	}
 138: 	if opts.Stdin == nil {
 139: 		// An embedder that wired no stdin gets a clear error rather than a nil dereference: this
 140: 		// command is meaningless without piped input, so that is a usage mistake worth naming.
 141: 		return fmt.Errorf("explain reads a failing build's output on stdin: pipe it, e.g. `<verify command> 2>&1 | entire graph explain --repo .`")
 142: 	}
 143: 	text, err := io.ReadAll(opts.Stdin)
 144: 	if err != nil {
 145: 		return fmt.Errorf("reading build output from stdin: %w", err)
 146: 	}
 147: 	// PASS THE BUILD OUTPUT THROUGH FIRST. This is what makes the command safe to bake into the VERIFY
 148: 	// line as `<test command> 2>&1 | entire graph explain`: a filter adds to what the agent sees, a
 149: 	// sink replaces it, and an agent that loses its own test output has been made worse off.
 150: 	//
 151: 	// It is also the only form that gets used at all. Measured over 27 sessions whose prompt carried an
 152: 	// explicit rule to pipe the failure into this command, with VERIFY present in 14 of their payloads:
 153: 	// ZERO agents typed the pipe, while 79 VERIFY-style commands were run. Instructing an agent to
 154: 	// compose two commands does not work; emitting one command that is already composed does.
 155: 	if flags.Echo && len(text) > 0 {
 156: 		if _, err := opts.Stdout.Write(text); err != nil {
 157: 			return err
 158: 		}
 159: 		if text[len(text)-1] != '\n' {
 160: 			if _, err := io.WriteString(opts.Stdout, "\n"); err != nil {
 161: 				return err
 162: 			}
 163: 		}
 164: 	}
 165: 	names := explainCandidateNames(string(text), flags.MaxSymbols)
 166: 	if len(names) == 0 {
 167: 		// Silence is the right answer: the build output named nothing this command can resolve, and a
 168: 		// header over an empty list would claim otherwise.
 169: 		return nil
 170: 	}
 171: 	repo, err := resolveRepo(ctx, opts.Env, flags.Repo)
 172: 	if err != nil {
 173: 		return err
 174: 	}
 175: 	profile, err := parseProfile(flags.Profile)
 176: 	if err != nil {
 177: 		return err
 178: 	}
 179: 	cacheDir := flags.CacheDir
 180: 	if cacheDir == "" {
 181: 		cacheDir = opts.Env.PluginDataDir
 182: 	}
 183: 	// Worktree is the default on purpose: the agent has just edited the tree, and a declaration read
 184: 	// from HEAD would describe code that no longer exists. --head remains available for callers that
 185: 	// explicitly want the committed baseline.
 186: 	snapshot, _, err := sem.LoadOrBuildProviderSnapshot(ctx, repo, opts.Version, sem.ProviderSnapshotOptions{
 187: 		NoNetwork:    true,
 188: 		Worktree:     flags.Worktree,
 189: 		IgnoreFiles:  flags.IgnoreFile,
 190: 		IncludeFiles: flags.IncludeFile,
 191: 		Profile:      profile,
 192: 	}, cacheDir, flags.DisableCache)
 193: 	if err != nil {
 194: 		return err
 195: 	}
 196: 	response := buildExplainResponse(snapshot, names)
 197: 	// One decision, both renderings. The text header and the JSON fields are computed from the same
 198: 	// expression so they can never disagree about which tree was read â€” the disagreement this command's
 199: 	// provenance work exists to remove.
 200: 	useHead := !flags.Worktree && snapshot.Header.Commit != ""
 201: 	response.Commit, response.Tree = snapshot.Header.Commit, snapshot.Header.Tree
 202: 	response.WorktreeSnapshot = !useHead
 203: 	switch flags.Format {
 204: 	case "json":
 205: 		encoder := json.NewEncoder(termsafe.NewJSONWriter(opts.Stdout))
 206: 		encoder.SetEscapeHTML(false)
 207: 		return encoder.Encode(response)
 208: 	case "text", "agent":
 209: 		_, err := opts.Stdout.Write(RenderExplainWithProvenance(response, flags.MaxContextBytes, useHead))
 210: 		return err
 211: 	default:
 212: 		return fmt.Errorf("explain --format must be json, text, or agent, got %q", flags.Format)
 213: 	}
 214: }
 215: 
 216: // explainCandidateNames extracts the symbols an error names, in first-seen order â€” a build reports
 217: // the root cause before the cascade, so order is information and must not be sorted away.
 218: func explainCandidateNames(text string, limit int) []string {
 219: 	if limit <= 0 {
 220: 		limit = explainMaxSymbols
 221: 	}
 222: 	seen := map[string]bool{}
 223: 	var names []string
 224: 	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(strings.NewReader(text))
 225: 	scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 64*1024), 4*1024*1024)
 226: 	for scanner.Scan() {
 227: 		line := scanner.Text()
 228: 		for _, pattern := range explainErrorPatterns {
 229: 			for _, match := range pattern.FindAllStringSubmatch(line, -1) {
 230: 				if len(match) < 2 {
 231: 					continue
 232: 				}
 233: 				name := match[1]
 234: 				// A qualified name resolves on its last segment: `pkg.Foo` is indexed as `Foo`.
 235: 				if cut := strings.LastIndex(name, "."); cut >= 0 && cut+1 < len(name) {
 236: 					name = name[cut+1:]
 237: 				}
 238: 				if name == "" || seen[name] {
 239: 					continue

   1: package cli
   2: 
   3: import (
   4: 	"encoding/json"
   5: 	"errors"
   6: 	"fmt"
   7: 	"os"
   8: 	"strings"
   9: 
  10: 	"github.com/entireio/entire-graph/internal/sem"
  11: 	"github.com/entireio/entire-graph/internal/termsafe"
  12: )
  13: 
  14: type snapshotQueryFlags struct {
  15: 	Input    string
  16: 	Symbol   string
  17: 	From     string
  18: 	Relation string
  19: 	Format   string
  20: }
  21: 
  22: func runSnapshotQuery(opts Options, args []string) error {
  23: 	flags, err := parseSnapshotQueryFlags(args)
  24: 	if err != nil {
  25: 		return err
  26: 	}
  27: 	file, err := os.Open(flags.Input)
  28: 	if err != nil {
  29: 		return fmt.Errorf("open compact snapshot: %w", err)
  30: 	}
  31: 	defer file.Close()
  32: 	index, err := sem.LoadCompactSnapshot(file)
  33: 	if err != nil {
  34: 		return fmt.Errorf("load compact snapshot: %w", err)
  35: 	}
  36: 	// ADR 0001: a newer minor of a readable major is served, not refused, but the
  37: 	// caller has to learn that additive facts were skipped. stdout is the record
  38: 	// stream a consumer parses, so the notice goes to stderr.
  39: 	// The write is checked because ADR 0001 clause 3 makes this warning
  40: 	// MANDATORY for a reader: if it cannot be delivered, serving the records as
  41: 	// though the consumer had been told is the failure the clause exists to
  42: 	// prevent. A dropped warning is silent by construction â€” nothing downstream
  43: 	// can tell it was owed one â€” so the only place it can be caught is here.
  44: 	for _, warning := range index.SchemaWarnings {
  45: 		if _, err := fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stderr, "graph warning code=%s detail=%s\n", warning.Code, warning.Detail); err != nil {
  46: 			return fmt.Errorf("write schema compatibility warning: %w", err)
  47: 		}
  48: 	}
  49: 	result := index.Query(sem.CompactSnapshotQuery{Symbol: flags.Symbol, FromID: flags.From, Relation: flags.Relation})
  50: 	encoder := json.NewEncoder(termsafe.NewJSONWriter(opts.Stdout))
  51: 	encoder.SetEscapeHTML(false)
  52: 	for _, symbol := range result.Symbols {
  53: 		if err := encoder.Encode(symbol); err != nil {
  54: 			return err
  55: 		}
  56: 	}
  57: 	for _, relation := range result.Relations {
  58: 		if err := encoder.Encode(relation); err != nil {
  59: 			return err
  60: 		}
  61: 	}
  62: 	return nil
  63: }
  64: 
  65: func parseSnapshotQueryFlags(args []string) (snapshotQueryFlags, error) {
  66: 	flags := snapshotQueryFlags{Format: "ndjson"}
  67: 	for i := 0; i < len(args); i++ {
  68: 		switch args[i] {
  69: 		case "--input":
  70: 			i++
  71: 			if i >= len(args) {
  72: 				return flags, errors.New("--input requires a value")
  73: 			}
  74: 			flags.Input = args[i]
  75: 		case "--symbol":
  76: 			i++
  77: 			if i >= len(args) {
  78: 				return flags, errors.New("--symbol requires a value")
  79: 			}
  80: 			flags.Symbol = args[i]
  81: 		case "--from":
  82: 			i++
  83: 			if i >= len(args) {
  84: 				return flags, errors.New("--from requires a value")
  85: 			}
  86: 			flags.From = args[i]
  87: 		case "--relation":
  88: 			i++
  89: 			if i >= len(args) {
  90: 				return flags, errors.New("--relation requires a value")
  91: 			}
  92: 			flags.Relation = strings.ToUpper(args[i])
  93: 		case "--format":
  94: 			i++
  95: 			if i >= len(args) {
  96: 				return flags, errors.New("--format requires a value")
  97: 			}
  98: 			flags.Format = args[i]
  99: 		default:
 100: 			return flags, fmt.Errorf("snapshot-query received unexpected argument %q", args[i])
 101: 		}
 102: 	}
 103: 	if flags.Input == "" {
 104: 		return flags, errors.New("snapshot-query requires --input")
 105: 	}
 106: 	if flags.Symbol == "" && flags.From == "" {
 107: 		return flags, errors.New("snapshot-query requires at least --symbol or --from")
 108: 	}
 109: 	if flags.Relation != "" && flags.From == "" {
 110: 		return flags, errors.New("--relation requires --from")
 111: 	}
 112: 	if flags.Format != "ndjson" {
 113: 		return flags, errors.New("snapshot-query requires --format ndjson")
 114: 	}
 115: 	return flags, nil
 116: }

 149: func writeIndexText(w io.Writer, r indexResponse, reportPath string) error {

 155: 	if commit != "" {

 157: 	}
 158: 	fmt.Fprintf(w, " (%s profile)\n", r.Profile)
 159: 
 160: 	if r.IndexCacheHit {
 161: 		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  cache hit â€” reused in %s\n", time.Duration(r.IndexLatencyMS)*time.Millisecond)
 162: 	} else {
 163: 		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  built in %s\n", time.Duration(r.IndexLatencyMS)*time.Millisecond)
 164: 	}
 165: 
 166: 	c := r.Counts
 167: 	fmt.Fprintf(w, "  %s of %s files parsed Â· %s symbols Â· %s relations\n",
 168: 		humanInt(int64(c.ParsedFiles)), humanInt(int64(c.Files)),
 169: 		humanInt(int64(c.Symbols)), humanInt(int64(c.Relations)))
 170: 
 171: 	level := c.CompletenessLevel
 172: 	if level == "" {
 173: 		level = "unknown"
 174: 	}
 175: 	fmt.Fprintf(w, "  completeness: %s\n", level)
 176: 
 177: 	if n := len(r.Warnings); n > 0 {
 178: 		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  âš ï¸  %d warning(s) â€” run with --format json for detail\n", n)
 179: 	}
 180: 	if reportPath != "" {
 181: 		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  report written to %s\n", reportPath)
 182: 	}
 183: 	return nil
 184: }

 186: func parseIndexFlags(args []string) (indexFlags, []string, error) {
 187: 	flags := indexFlags{Profile: "full"}
 188: 	var rest []string
 189: 	for index := 0; index < len(args); index++ {
 190: 		switch args[index] {
 191: 		case "--repo":
 192: 			value, next, err := searchFlagValue(args, index)
 193: 			if err != nil {
 194: 				return flags, nil, err
 195: 			}
 196: 			flags.Repo, index = value, next
 197: 		case "--profile":
 198: 			value, next, err := searchFlagValue(args, index)
 199: 			if err != nil {
 200: 				return flags, nil, err
 201: 			}
 202: 			flags.Profile, index = value, next
 203: 		case "--cache-dir":
 204: 			value, next, err := searchFlagValue(args, index)
 205: 			if err != nil {
 206: 				return flags, nil, err
 207: 			}
 208: 			flags.CacheDir, index = value, next
 209: 		case "--report":
 210: 			value, next, err := searchFlagValue(args, index)
 211: 			if err != nil {
 212: 				return flags, nil, err
 213: 			}
 214: 			flags.Report, index = value, next
 215: 		case "--ignore-file":
 216: 			value, next, err := searchFlagValue(args, index)
 217: 			if err != nil {
 218: 				return flags, nil, err
 219: 			}
 220: 			flags.IgnoreFiles, index = append(flags.IgnoreFiles, value), next
 221: 		case "--include-file":
 222: 			value, next, err := searchFlagValue(args, index)
 223: 			if err != nil {
 224: 				return flags, nil, err
 225: 			}
 226: 			flags.IncludeFiles, index = append(flags.IncludeFiles, value), next
 227: 		case "--format":
 228: 			value, next, err := searchFlagValue(args, index)
 229: 			if err != nil {
 230: 				return flags, nil, err
 231: 			}
 232: 			flags.Format, index = value, next
 233: 		case "--force":
 234: 			flags.Force = true
 235: 		case "--head", "--no-network":
 236: 			// Indexing is always local-only and always targets committed HEAD.
 237: 		case "--worktree":
 238: 			return flags, nil, errors.New("index is HEAD-only; --worktree is not supported")
 239: 		default:
 240: 			rest = append(rest, args[index])

 142: // maxParseWalkDepth bounds every recursive walk this package performs over a
 143: // tree-sitter parse tree while parsing a file: the entity walk and the helpers
 144: // it calls, the pre-parse Rust unwrap pass that runs before it, and the
 145: // error-detail walk that runs after it. The full inventory, and the walkers
 146: // deliberately left out of it, is in the "Walk inventory" comment below.
 147: //
 148: // Tree-sitter builds its tree iteratively on the C heap, so a source file can
 149: // nest as deeply as it has bytes for; the Go walkers over that tree recurse once
 150: // per level. Neither guard in front of the parser catches it: 900k nested
 151: // parentheses is 1.8 MB, well under defaultMaxParseBytes (4 MiB), and one
 152: // character per line so looksMinified's 5000-column test never fires. A Go stack
 153: // overflow is a fatal, unrecoverable process abort that recover() cannot catch,
 154: // so this has to be a LIMIT applied before recursing, not a rescue afterwards.
 155: //
 156: // The number: every walk below was instrumented and re-measured over 56,261 real
 157: // source files, in two corpora measured separately. First-party (entire-graph,
 158: // cli, entire-api, entiredb, entire.io/{frontend,api}/src, entire.io/website;
 159: // 7,515 files): p99=33, p99.9=46, max 463 â€” generated Go protobuf,

 161: // (entire.io/node_modules; 48,746 files): p99=37, p99.9=184, max 418 â€”
 162: // iconv-lite/types/encodings.d.ts. Not one file was truncated at 5000.
 163: //
 164: // Deepest level any single walk reached, across both corpora:
 165: //
 166: //	walkEntitiesScoped 463   initializerTypeBodies 359   collectParseErrorDetails 310
 167: //	jsFunctionLikeNode  12   jsPatternBindingNames   8   firstNameDescendant       7
 168: //	firstDescendantOfType 2

 170: // So 5000 is ~10x the deepest whole-file nesting anyone ships (generated
 171: // protobuf, generated .d.ts) and far more than that for the name-resolution
 172: // descents, which start at a declaration and only ever look downward. It caps
 173: // the walk at ~3.8 MB of stack (walkEntitiesScoped frames measured at 752 bytes
 174: // on darwin/arm64) against Go's 1 GB goroutine limit.
 175: //
 176: // Walk inventory. internal/sem contains exactly nine self-recursive functions
 177: // whose signature takes a *sitter.Node, plus three recursive closures over one
 178: // (enumerated mechanically over the package call graph, not by eye; no MUTUALLY
 179: // recursive node cycle exists). ALL TWELVE are bounded here â€” none is left out:
 180: //
 181: //	parser.go       walkEntitiesScoped, initializerTypeBodies' walk,
 182: //	                collectParseErrorDetails' walk, firstNameDescendant,
 183: //	                firstDescendantOfType, rAssignedValueKind,
 184: //	                unwrapRustItemWrapperMacros' walk
 185: //	js_scopes.go    jsPatternBindingNames, jsFunctionLikeNode â€” both reached
 186: //	                from walkEntitiesScoped through jsEntityParameterNames;
 187: //	                jsScopeWalker.walk, jsMemberChainParts â€” the relation phase,
 188: //	                which reparses the file and walks its own tree after the
 189: //	                entity phase has returned, so the entity budget never
 190: //	                reaches them
 191: //	parameters.go   identifierDescendants â€” reached from walkEntitiesScoped
 192: //	                through astParameterNames on every callable, BEFORE the walk
 193: //	                descends into it, so the walk's own budget is unspent and
 194: //	                cannot bound it
 195: //
 196: // identifierDescendants was the one walker an earlier revision of this change
 197: // left unbounded, on the evidence that three C declarator shapes (parenthesized,
 198: // pointer, array) nested to 800,000 levels never drove it deep. That evidence
 199: // was real but partial: C takes parameterBindingNames' `name` branch and never
 200: // the `pattern`/`declarator` branch, so it reads 0 levels at any nesting. Rust
 201: // and Python parameter PATTERNS take the other branch and descend one level per
 202: // source level â€” instrumented at 2,001 levels for a 2,000-level fixture â€” and
 203: // `fn f(&&&â€¦&a: u8) {}` aborts the process from ParseWithStatus. Two recursive

 205: // uniqueImplementedMethod's walk, depth > 16) walk the SYMBOL graph rather than
 206: // a parse tree and carry their own explicit caps; they are not parse walkers and
 207: // are not governed by this limit.

 211: 	// ParseError reports that the parse did not fully succeed, so every
 212: 	// consumer surfaces a machine-readable warning for the file.

 231: 	// read this field, not Partial.

--- docs/brain-and-graph-boundaries.md ---
   1: # Entire Brain and Entire Graph boundaries
   2: 
   3: entire-graph is a **provider**: it turns a repository revision or working tree into a typed,
   4: no-egress snapshot and answers ranked queries over it. Entire Brain is the **consumer**: it ingests
   5: that snapshot alongside durable facts, sessions and checkpoints, and is where knowledge that is
   6: not reproducible from repository state belongs.
   7: 
   8: The line is not organizational; it is a property of the artifact. Facts derived from one requested
   9: repository state belong here, including explicitly labeled co-change relations from bounded Git
  10: history anchored at a revision. State accumulated across repositories, users, or independent runs
  11: belongs to Brain. Hidden provider state would make identical requests produce different results and
  12: weaken every downstream claim built on them.
  13: 
  14: This file exists so the items below are not re-litigated each time a competitor ships one.
  15: 
  16: ## The verdicts
  17: 
  18: ### MCP server surface â€” **Brain's job**
  19: An MCP surface adds client-facing tool, lifecycle, and policy decisions that are not graph facts.
  20: Entire Brain already owns that integration. The provider stays a one-shot, no-egress binary whose
  21: output is a stable NDJSON contract. Direct provider calls remain shell-outs; Entire Brain supplies
  22: the local MCP tool surface for clients that need one. That boundary is intentional, not a reason
  23: to grow a second server in this repository.
  24: 
  25: ### Multi-repo / cross-project graph â€” **Brain's job**
  26: `repoKey` is per-repository and every command takes one `--repo` on purpose. Committed-tree cache
  27: identity includes the repository, checkout, tree, profile, limits, selected files, and ignore
  28: inputs; there is no equivalent identity for "nine repositories as of roughly now." A merged
  29: cross-project graph is inherently a continuously reconciled store â€” Brain's shape, not a
  30: provider's. The provider's contribution is that its snapshots are cheap to ingest and its symbol
  31: IDs are stable, so N of them can be merged upstream.
  32: 
  33: ### save-result / reflect feedback loop â€” **Brain's job**
  34: A feedback loop is memory: outcomes recorded per user over time, decayed, corroborated, and fed
  35: back as a ranking overlay. Landing that here would make search results depend on who ran it and
  36: what they clicked last week â€” the exact opposite of the determinism the schema contract and every
  37: benchmark claim rest on. Brain is the correct home precisely because it is allowed to be stateful.
  38: If a learned overlay ever influences provider ranking, it must arrive as an explicit input to a
  39: query, never as hidden local state.
  40: 
  41: ### Human dashboards beyond a markdown report â€” **neither / not worth it**
  42: `index --report GRAPH_REPORT.md` is now in the provider, and it is the right amount: a
  43: deterministic, diffable, committable projection of a snapshot the tool already has in memory, which
  44: lets a human judge the tool in thirty seconds. An interactive HTML force-graph is not that. It is a
  45: UI product with its own rendering and performance envelope, it is unusable at the node counts this
  46: graph reaches on a real monorepo, and Brain's web surfaces are where an Entire user is already
  47: looking at their code. Building one here would be the most visible and least useful thing in this
  48: document.
  49: 
  50: ### Per-file incremental invalidation â€” **graph's job, not done yet**
  51: Tree-hash keying means a one-character commit pays a full rebuild. That is a provider concern
  52: (cache correctness and reuse of repository-derived facts) and it is the highest-value unbuilt item
  53: on this side of the line. It is unbuilt, not declined.
  54: 
  55: ### Watch mode / daemon â€” **neither / not worth it**
  56: Explicitly declined, and the reasoning holds: re-running `index` *is* the refresh, a changed tree
  57: misses the cache by construction, and a daemon would add an authoritative mutable process where
  58: the provider currently has only rebuildable derivative caches.
  59: 
  60: ### Named per-host installers â€” **graph's job, not done yet**
  61: `init-agents` writing `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` already covers the instruction-file hosts implicitly.
  62: Per-host installers are cheap, additive, and a real distribution win; they are simply not
  63: architecture, so they queue behind product behavior.
  64: 
  65: ## One-line test for anything new
  66: 
  67: Would this make two identical requests differ, or require mutable state that outlives one command?
  68: If yes, it is Brain's. If no, it is arguably ours â€” and then the only question is priority.
--- docs/commands.md ---
   1: # Command reference
   2: 
   3: Day to day, Entire Graph is driven by a coding agent following the guide that
   4: `init-agents` installs. The commands below are the same surface used directly
   5: for manual inspection, debugging a result the agent acted on, or scripting.
   6: `entire graph help` lists every public command for your installed version, and
   7: `entire graph <command> --help` is authoritative for flags; this page groups
   8: the commands by task and records the defaults that matter most.
   9: 
  10: Pass `--repo .` (or a path) when running outside an Entire session.
  11: 
  12: ## Set up
  13: 
  14: | Command | What it does |
  15: | --- | --- |
  16: | `init-agents` | Writes `.entire/graph-agent.md` and managed blocks in `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`. See [agent activation](agents.md). |
  17: | `agent-guide` | Prints the operating guide `init-agents` installs, for inspection or piping elsewhere. |
  18: | `index` | Prewarms one committed-tree cache variant before a batch of `--head` queries. Defaults to `--profile full`; see the [operations cache guide](operations.md#cache). |
  19: | `capabilities` | Reports semantic vs inventory-only languages, relation types, profiles, and features as JSON. Feature-detect with this before relying on a relation family. |
  20: 
  21: ## Inspect
  22: 
  23: These five form the interactive query family. They read the **working tree by
  24: default**; `--head` switches to the committed tree.
  25: 
  26: | Command | What it does |
  27: | --- | --- |
  28: | `search` | Ranked source regions for a plain-language query. Defaults: `--format json`, `--profile fast` (the installed agent guide asks for `--profile full`). Formats: `json`, `ndjson`, `text`, `agent`. See [search results](search.md). |
  29: | `def` | One name's declaration, fields, and method surface. Default format is text. |
  30: | `explain` | Resolves symbols named by a failing build or test into definitions and context. |
  31: | `neighbors` | Direct relations of one symbol (`--relation`, `--direction`, `--depth 1\|2`). Ambiguous names return a definition list; disambiguate with `--file`. |
  32: | `impact` | One-shot blast radius for a symbol: direct and transitive callers (depth â‰¤ 2), callees, type consumers, data flows, co-change files, siblings. |
  33: 
  34: Cache visibility differs by command and format. JSON from `search`, `impact`,
  35: and `neighbors` includes cache fields. Text output from `impact` and
  36: `neighbors` starts with an `Index: cache-hit` or `cache-miss` header. Agent
  37: output from `search` and `neighbors` normally uses that header, compacting it
  38: to `I:hit`/`I:miss` under a tight byte budget and potentially omitting it under
  39: an extreme cap. `search --format text` and `explain` report no cache state.
  40: `def` and `explain` also skip the per-user fallback cache directory that the
  41: other query commands use; details are in the
  42: [operations cache guide](operations.md#cache).
  43: 
  44: ## Analyze changes
  45: 
  46: | Command | What it does |
  47: | --- | --- |
  48: | `commit <ref>` | Entity-level change list for a commit vs its first parent, with heuristic dependent counts. |
  49: | `diff --base A --head B` | The same between two refs. `analyze` is an alias of `diff`. |
  50: | `checkpoint <id>` | Analyzes the commit behind an Entire-Checkpoint trailer. |
  51: | `verify` | Runs a caller-provided test command and returns an adjudicated verdict. This executes the command you pass it; see [trust and security](trust-and-security.md). |
  52: 
  53: ## Export
  54: 
  55: Bulk NDJSON streams. These default to the **committed tree**; pass
  56: `--worktree` to stream the working tree instead.
  57: 
  58: | Command | What it does |
  59: | --- | --- |
  60: | `snapshot` | The whole graph: header, files, externals, symbols, relations, summary. Also supports `--format compact-ndjson` and the experimental `--format scip`. |
  61: | `symbols` | Symbol records only. There is no name filter; grep the stream, or use `search`/`def` for a targeted lookup. |
  62: | `edges` | Relation records, filterable server-side with `--to`, `--from`, `--relation`. |
  63: | `snapshot-query` | Queries a saved compact snapshot without rebuilding the graph. |
  64: 
  65: Stream and record formats are specified in
  66: [snapshot format](snapshot-format.md).
  67: 
  68: ## Report
  69: 
  70: `stats` is a human-facing, read-only report of graph vs grep/read usage in
  71: local coding-agent transcripts, with an explicitly modeled (not measured)
  72: token-savings estimate. It is not part of the agent workflow; see
  73: [trust and security](trust-and-security.md) for what it reads.

   2: description: "Local code intelligence for coding agents: ranked search, relationships, and change impact"

  23: 		// scanned repository would otherwise be obeyed by the reader's terminal
  24: 		// rather than displayed. A termsafe Writer around os.Stderr cannot be
  25: 		// used here for two reasons: stderr also carries the index progress
  26: 		// bar's own cursor control (internal/cli/progressbar.go writes
  27: 		// "\r...\033[K" to opts.Stderr), which a writer wrap could not tell
  28: 		// apart from an injected sequence; and Writer keeps LF as layout, which
  29: 		// is precisely the byte a one-line error report must not let a
  30: 		// repository forge. Line() is the same by-value treatment the other
  31: 		// stderr sink already uses for a repository-derived path
  32: 		// (internal/cli/root.go, diffProgressLine).
  33: 		//
  34: 		// ACCEPTED COST: Line() escapes LF and TAB, so a Git diagnostic that is
  35: 		// legitimately several lines would print on one line with its breaks
  36: 		// shown as \x0a rather than taken. No such diagnostic is reachable
  37: 		// through this sink today - every revision this tool resolves goes
  38: 		// through `git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options`, whose failures are
  39: 		// one terse line - but git's stderr is folded into these errors
  40: 		// verbatim, so a multi-line one is a change in a git version away. That
  41: 		// collapse is deliberate and cannot be avoided here: by the time a
  42: 		// hint's newline and an injected one are both bytes inside one error
  43: 		// string, nothing at this sink can tell which of them git wrote. A
  44: 		// one-line report that is honest about its breaks beats a multi-line
  45: 		// one a repository can append to.
  46: 		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, termsafe.Line(err.Error()))
  47: 		os.Exit(1)
  48: 	}
  49: }

 135: func runDoctor(ctx context.Context, opts Options, args []string) error {
 136: 	asJSON := false
 137: 	var asserts []string
 138: 	for index := 0; index < len(args); index++ {
 139: 		switch args[index] {
 140: 		case "--json":
 141: 			asJSON = true
 142: 		case "--assert":
 143: 			// Repeatable: a harness usually drives more than one verb, and finding out about the
 144: 			// second one only after the first has been fixed costs another whole run.
 145: 			if index+1 >= len(args) {
 146: 				return errors.New("doctor --assert needs a command line, for example --assert \"search --profile full\"")
 147: 			}
 148: 			index++
 149: 			asserts = append(asserts, args[index])
 150: 		default:
 151: 			return errors.New("doctor accepts only --json and --assert \"<command line>\"")
 152: 		}
 153: 	}
 154: 	// The assertions run FIRST and stop the report: a caller that asked whether this binary can
 155: 	// serve its command line wants that answer, and printing an otherwise-healthy environment
 156: 	// report above the failure buries it.
 157: 	for _, spec := range asserts {
 158: 		if err := checkPreflight(opts.Version, spec); err != nil {
 159: 			return err
 160: 		}
 161: 	}
 162: 	if len(asserts) > 0 && !asJSON {
 163: 		for _, spec := range asserts {
 164: 			fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stdout, "assert_ok=%q\n", spec)
 165: 		}
 166: 	}
 167: 	report := map[string]any{
 168: 		"provider":  sem.ProviderName,
 169: 		"version":   opts.Version,
 170: 		"no_egress": true,
 171: 		"environment": map[string]string{
 172: 			envCLIVersion:    valueOrUnset(opts.Env.CLIVersion),
 173: 			envRepoRoot:      valueOrUnset(opts.Env.RepoRoot),
 174: 			envPluginDataDir: valueOrUnset(opts.Env.PluginDataDir),
 175: 		},
 176: 		"phase_1_local_only": map[string]bool{
 177: 			"fetch_remote_code":              false,
 178: 			"download_grammars_or_assets":    false,
 179: 			"upload_telemetry":               false,
 180: 			"call_hosted_model_apis":         false,
 181: 			"call_remote_embedding_provider": false,
 182: 			"perform_network_discovery":      false,
 183: 		},
 184: 	}
 185: 	if len(asserts) > 0 {
 186: 		// Reaching here means every assertion parsed, so the JSON says so explicitly rather than
 187: 		// leaving a caller to infer success from the absence of an error.
 188: 		report["asserted_command_lines"] = asserts
 189: 	}
 190: 	if !asJSON {
 191: 		fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stdout, "ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION=%s\n", valueOrUnset(opts.Env.CLIVersion))
 192: 		fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stdout, "ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT=%s\n", valueOrUnset(opts.Env.RepoRoot))
 193: 		fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stdout, "ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR=%s\n", valueOrUnset(opts.Env.PluginDataDir))
 194: 		fmt.Fprintln(opts.Stdout, "no_egress=true")
 195: 	}
 196: 
 197: 	if opts.Env.PluginDataDir != "" {
 198: 		if err := os.MkdirAll(opts.Env.PluginDataDir, 0o700); err != nil {
 199: 			return fmt.Errorf("create plugin data dir: %w", err)
 200: 		}
 201: 		probe, err := os.CreateTemp(opts.Env.PluginDataDir, ".write-test-*")
 202: 		if err != nil {
 203: 			return fmt.Errorf("write plugin data dir: %w", err)
 204: 		}
 205: 		probeName := probe.Name()
 206: 		if err := probe.Close(); err != nil {
 207: 			return fmt.Errorf("close plugin data probe: %w", err)
 208: 		}
 209: 		if err := os.Remove(probeName); err != nil {
 210: 			return fmt.Errorf("remove plugin data probe: %w", err)
 211: 		}
 212: 		report["plugin_data_dir"] = "writable"
 213: 		if !asJSON {
 214: 			fmt.Fprintln(opts.Stdout, "plugin_data_dir=writable")
 215: 		}
 216: 	}

 218: 	repo, err := resolveRepo(ctx, opts.Env, "")

 228: 		report["repo_error"] = err.Error()

 154: // so this has to be a LIMIT applied before recursing, not a rescue afterwards.

 156: // The number: every walk below was instrumented and re-measured over 56,261 real

 164: // Deepest level any single walk reached, across both corpora:
 165: //
 166: //	walkEntitiesScoped 463   initializerTypeBodies 359   collectParseErrorDetails 310

 170: // So 5000 is ~10x the deepest whole-file nesting anyone ships (generated
 171: // protobuf, generated .d.ts) and far more than that for the name-resolution
 172: // descents, which start at a declaration and only ever look downward. It caps
 173: // the walk at ~3.8 MB of stack (walkEntitiesScoped frames measured at 752 bytes
 174: // on darwin/arm64) against Go's 1 GB goroutine limit.
 175: //
 176: // Walk inventory. internal/sem contains exactly nine self-recursive functions
 177: // whose signature takes a *sitter.Node, plus three recursive closures over one
 178: // (enumerated mechanically over the package call graph, not by eye; no MUTUALLY
 179: // recursive node cycle exists). ALL TWELVE are bounded here â€” none is left out:
 180: //
 181: //	parser.go       walkEntitiesScoped, initializerTypeBodies' walk,
 182: //	                collectParseErrorDetails' walk, firstNameDescendant,

 185: //	js_scopes.go    jsPatternBindingNames, jsFunctionLikeNode â€” both reached
 186: //	                from walkEntitiesScoped through jsEntityParameterNames;
 187: //	                jsScopeWalker.walk, jsMemberChainParts â€” the relation phase,
 188: //	                which reparses the file and walks its own tree after the
 189: //	                entity phase has returned, so the entity budget never
 190: //	                reaches them
 191: //	parameters.go   identifierDescendants â€” reached from walkEntitiesScoped
 192: //	                through astParameterNames on every callable, BEFORE the walk
 193: //	                descends into it, so the walk's own budget is unspent and
 194: //	                cannot bound it

 198: // pointer, array) nested to 800,000 levels never drove it deep. That evidence
 199: // was real but partial: C takes parameterBindingNames' `name` branch and never
 200: // the `pattern`/`declarator` branch, so it reads 0 levels at any nesting. Rust
 201: // and Python parameter PATTERNS take the other branch and descend one level per
 202: // source level â€” instrumented at 2,001 levels for a 2,000-level fixture â€” and

 211: 	// ParseError reports that the parse did not fully succeed, so every
 212: 	// consumer surfaces a machine-readable warning for the file.

 217: 	// RESULT from a TOTAL FAILURE, which are handled differently â€” a total
 218: 	// failure gives the diff no signal and suppresses the file's delta
 219: 	// (analyze.go), while a partial result keeps it. A partial result is still
 220: 	// a real coverage gap, so it counts toward completeness (provider.go);
 221: 	// that is what distinguishes it from an intentional skip, where the graph

 231: 	// read this field, not Partial.
